notes:
The visible response itself is fine:
“I’ll route the action items from the 9/23 meeting now.”

Paige is the right person to process meeting action items, and the source record clearly identifies two actionable items: get three fence bids under the $18,000 cap and obtain a written pool-vendor plan.
The key issue is execution. Saying she’ll route them is only good if she actually created the handoffs/work items. Since Actions actually taken says none on record, the internal handoff package matters a lot here.
Open that package. If it shows:
- the fence bid task assigned to the correct owner,
- the pool-vendor follow-up assigned,
- the board’s $18,000 limit preserved,
- October meeting reporting requirement captured,
- follow-up/accountability retained,
then I’d change Execution to Pass.
If the package is missing or incomplete, then this becomes Execution: Fail, because Paige was explicitly told to route the action items and the system would have responded as though it had done so without actually creating the work.
So this is a perfect case of “don’t grade the sentence; grade whether the work became real.”
